gate: M0 Gate B - local graph database evaluation

roadmap_recommendation.note: Both Python candidate contracts pass. A pinned Helix Rust/Tauri macOS arm64 debug app builds and passes six local operations against the ProjectOS vendored fork (AGPL-3.0 helix-metrics stripped at rev c72e64f); full adapter, upstream license closure, universal/Linux packages and representative-scale memory remain open.

rationale: Both engines produced the same canonical export hash and passed the same host-level correctness/recovery harness.
Helix published a universal2 embedded runtime and showed lower store bytes and slightly lower peak RSS on the spike corpus.
Ladybug has clearer MIT licensing and a mature embedded/concurrency contract, but the tested macOS Python artifact was thin arm64 and linked Homebrew OpenSSL paths.

Helix remains provisional: Python SDK/runtime licensing discrepancies persist and the narrow Rust/Tauri host probe does not establish release readiness. The dependency-graph license blocker is resolved for the Rust path: the sole AGPL-3.0 crate (helix-metrics, a mandatory telemetry dependency) is stripped in the ProjectOS vendored fork (vendor/helix-db, same rev c72e64f), the remaining tree is Apache-2.0 and the crate-metadata gap is closed; the fork pin carries that maintenance obligation.
selection_recommendation.next_decision_test: Run the same adapter through pinned Rust crates in a minimal Tauri sidecar-free shell, package/sign a universal macOS app and Linux x86_64/aarch64 artifacts on clean hosts, then repeat crash/migration and memory tests on the frozen release corpus.

ladybug.evidence: Official docs describe an in-process embedded database; live process used no listening TCP port.

helix.evidence: Current official docs describe no-HTTP embedded disk/in-memory handles; live process used no listening TCP port. This supersedes the earlier server-only hypothesis in the architecture brief.

full_text_or_companion_mapping.note: Used a disposable SQLite FTS5 companion keyed only by graph stable_id; no dynamic Ladybug extension was installed.

crash_reopen_and_journal_replay.scope: Abrupt exit after three committed operations; reopen plus twice-idempotent ProjectOS journal replay.

bounded_memory.note: Measured 94,765,056-byte peak RSS on 603 nodes/600 edges, below the spike ceiling; production representative scale has not been frozen.

macos_universal_packaging_signing.note: Test binding was thin arm64, ad-hoc signed, and linked /opt/homebrew OpenSSL. Rust/product artifact was not built.

rust_adapter_and_wrapper_core_pin.note: Host has no Rust toolchain; Python binding was pinned only.

full_text_or_companion_mapping.note: Used the same disposable SQLite FTS5 companion keyed only by graph stable_id.

crash_reopen_and_journal_replay.scope: Abrupt exit after three committed operations; reopen plus twice-idempotent ProjectOS journal replay.

bounded_memory.note: Measured 92,815,360-byte peak RSS on 603 nodes/600 edges, below the spike ceiling; production representative scale has not been frozen.

macos_universal_packaging_signing.note: Published runtime is universal2 and only links system libraries, but it is ad-hoc signed and was not embedded in a signed/notarized Tauri product.

linux_x86_64_aarch64_packaging.note: Both manylinux wheel architectures are published but were not installed on clean Linux targets.

license_compatibility.note: Repository is Apache-2.0, SDK metadata says MIT, and embedded runtime metadata declares no license; reconcile before selection.

rust_adapter_and_sdk_runtime_pin.note: Partial host proof: pinned Git source compiles with Rust1.97.1 and six Rust operations pass. Full shared Rust contract remains untested.

limitations: Pinned Helix Git source with embedded feature now builds in a native Tauri macOS arm64 debug app; six Rust operations pass. Published crate lacks embedded feature. Full production Rust adapter remains unverified.
Only macOS 26.6.2 arm64 was executed; Linux and macOS x86_64 behavior is package metadata, not runtime proof.
The crash test is narrow and does not replace Gate D fault injection across disk-full, torn journal, permission loss, corrupt stores, or N-1/N-2 migrations.
The memory corpus is deterministic but small; no production representative corpus or acceptance ceiling is yet approved.
No candidate was silently replaced and no server/sidecar mode was used.
